# ADR-2 · ADR-022's references point at the wrong documents, and at one that does not exist

Found in review, then checked against every ADR's own title. ADR-022 is the ADR the WASI series leans on for its trust story, so a reader who follows its references lands in the wrong place — and one reference lands nowhere.

## The header: four labels, none matching its target

`ADR-022-binding-boundary.md:6-7`:

```
**Related:** ADR-012 (failure semantics), ADR-013 (who verifies), ADR-014 (portable slice and
pinned inputs), ADR-011 (crate identity and release train)
```

| cited | label given | that ADR actually is | the subject actually lives in |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADR-011 | crate identity and release train | **Approval Binding — Consequence-Bound Human Sign-Off** | `engine/.pi/architecture/CHANGELOG.md`; no ADR |
| ADR-012 | failure semantics | **Identity Attestation — OSS Attests, Enterprise Authorizes** | ADR-009 (Error Handling Pattern) |
| ADR-013 | who verifies | **Sequence Policy — Composed-Action Gating** | no ADR; ADR-012's "OSS attests, enterprise authorizes" is the nearest |
| ADR-014 | portable slice and pinned inputs | **Effect Identity Matching** | `docs/spike-portable-slice-2026-11.md`; no ADR |

ADR-023 (`:7-8`), ADR-011 (`:137`), ADR-014 (`:178`) and ADR-021 all use the correct labels, so this is one document's block, not a tree-wide drift. The fix is to state the real subjects — and where the subject has no ADR, to cite the document that has it, or to drop the reference rather than attach a wrong number to a right idea.

## The body: a citation to a section that exists nowhere

```
:47   the fifth operation (verification, ADR-013) is exactly how that surface grows
:65   ADR-012 tier 3 says a trap is fatal and host-visible, never rendered as a refusal or an allow
```

`grep -rn 'tier 3' engine/.pi docs` returns **only ADR-022's own line**. No ADR has tiers, and ADR-012 contains zero occurrences of "tier". So `:65` cites a section of a document that does not contain it — and `:142` repeats the same claim as `(ADR-012)`, which is the correct pointer only if the substance is in ADR-012 somewhere else.

`:47`'s parenthetical is the stale label again: ADR-013 is Sequence Policy; "verification" is not its subject.

This is the failure mode the ADR register exists to prevent, in the register itself: **a claim whose source cannot be checked is a claim.** The substantive statements may well be right — "a trap is not a refusal" is load-bearing and appears in ADR-022's title — but the citation must lead to the paragraph that says it.

## §6: "six rows" over a five-row table

`ADR-022-binding-boundary.md:134`:

> Every embedding language implements the same **six rows**.

The table directly beneath it has **five** rows, because `environ_sizes_get` / `environ_get` share one:

```
| environ_sizes_get / environ_get | … |
| clock_time_get                  | … |
| random_get                      | … |
| fd_write                        | … |
| proc_exit                       | … |
```

Six is the **import** count (`wasi/ci/imports.txt` has 6 entries), not the row count. The distinction is not pedantic: `wasi/ci/embedder-contract.json` carries **6** entries (one per import) while the prose table carries **5** (one per behaviour), so an implementer told "six rows" will look for a row the document does not have. `docs/binding-responsibility.md` gets this right in the same words — *"The module imports six functions"* and *"five claims, five owners"* — which is the phrasing ADR-022 should borrow.

## Acceptance

| # | Criterion | Command | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | no wrong labels | `python3 -` a check that every `ADR-nnn (label)` matches that ADR's title keyword | zero mismatches in ADR-022 |
| 2 | no dangling citation | `grep -rn 'tier 3' engine/.pi docs` | either a source, or the sentence rewritten |
| 3 | the count matches | the sentence and the table beneath it | "five rows" / "six imports", chosen deliberately |
| 4 | the fix is checked | the same label sweep over all ADRs | ADR-020/021's *descriptive* labels ("chained-log pattern") are allowed and named as such |
title: docs(adr): ADR-022 cites four wrong documents, one nonexistent section, and miscounts its own table
